answer: Admission is quota-limited: at most 1929 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the ivory. Flooding registration pushes an hostile operator to the back of the orchard queue while honest agents promoted earlier keep earning. The velvet index is deterministic from ledger replay, as a result nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
